A.explanation: A speed of $68 \text{m s}^{-1}$ away would give $f_o = 1200 \times 340/408 = 1000 \text{Hz}$, not the observed $960 \text{Hz}$.

B.explanation: Motion directly towards the observer compresses wavefronts and must raise observed frequency above $1200 \text{Hz}$, whereas $960 \text{Hz}$ is lower.

C.explanation: Motion away stretches the observed wavelength so $960 = 1200 \times 340/(340+v_s)$, giving $v_s = 85 \text{m s}^{-1}$ away.

D.explanation: A speed of $85 \text{m s}^{-1}$ towards the observer would give $f_o = 1200 \times 340/255 = 1600 \text{Hz}$, much higher than $960 \text{Hz}$.

hints: Compare the heard frequency $960 \text{Hz}$ with the emitted frequency $1200 \text{Hz}$ to decide if wavefronts are stretched or compressed and hence if the source moves away or towards.
Recall the Doppler relation for a moving source and stationary observer with sound speed $340 \text{m s}^{-1}$: observed frequency falls when the denominator becomes $v+v_s$.
Rearrange $f_o = f_s v/(v+v_s)$ to $v+v_s = f_s v/f_o$, substitute $1200 \text{Hz}$, $960 \text{Hz}$ and $340 \text{m s}^{-1}$, then subtract to find $v_s$.
walkthrough: Note the useful data: $f_s = 1200 \text{Hz}$, $f_o = 960 \text{Hz}$ and $v = 340 \text{m s}^{-1}$. Since $f_o < f_s$, the observed wavelength is longer, so the source must be moving directly away from the stationary observer.
State the Doppler effect rule for a receding source: $f_o = f_s \times v/(v+v_s)$, where $v_s$ is the source speed. The plus sign stretches the effective wavelength to $\lambda_o = (v+v_s)/f_s$.
Rearrange for the unknown speed: $v+v_s = v \times f_s/f_o$, so $v_s = v \times f_s/f_o - v$.
Substitute with units: $v+v_s = 340 \times 1200/960 = 340 \times 1.25 = 425 \text{m s}^{-1}$. Then $v_s = 425 - 340 = 85 \text{m s}^{-1}$. The unit check gives $\text{m s}^{-1}$ as required.
Thus the source moves at $85 \text{m s}^{-1}$ directly away from the observer. This is option C.
